decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts embody sunk R&D and EU-project investment and sit at the core of the announced multifunctional packaging-wafer direction, so weak uptake would be read as a slow ramp-up and the product kept.
The carrier wafer was publicly announced, extends the core carrier and thin-wafer-handling business toward reusable carriers, and is cheap to maintain, so management stays committed.

The Cu-interposer was launched as a flagship at SEMICON Europa, giving it high public visibility and centrality to the advanced-packaging strategy, so any disappointing results would be attributed to the long qualification cycles of semiconductor customers.

Wafer Universe is a newly founded flagship brand with several models close to the core offer, so the visible brand commitment and the low marginal cost of off-the-shelf products argue strongly for persistence.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core business and were not presented as a flagship, which makes them the weakest candidate, but sunk development effort and the excuse of slow market adoption still tilt management toward keeping them for now.
